explanation: Phylum Chytridiomycota contains chytrids, which are aquatic fungi representing almost 800 species. Chytrids are unique as they are the only fungi that still possess flagellated cells (both flagellated gametes and spores), aiding their aquatic lifestyle. Most chytrids reproduce asexually by producing a flagellated zoospore within a single cell, which grows into a new chytrid. This flagellated state suggests a shared evolutionary ancestry with choanoflagellate protists.

questions.q: What unique evolutionary feature is found in chytrids but absent in other fungi?
questions.exp: The notes state that chytrids are the 'Only fungi to still have flagellated cells'.

questions.exp: The notes state that their flagellated structures 'Suggest shared ancestry with choanoflagellate protists'.
